purpose: cross-world transfer of FROZEN models between two independently designed synthetic worlds — the defense against 'every number is on a world you wrote': signal that survives on a world the model never saw is generalization, not memorized world quirks

method.frozen: models are loaded from the source world's artifacts and never retrained or refit
method.recovery_metric: ROC-AUC + Brier of the frozen recovery head on the ENTIRE target dataset (all rows unseen)
method.action_value_metric: incremental net rupees of the frozen action head vs the deterministic rules baseline, graded by the target world's ground-truth value function on its time-ordered held-out split
method.determinism: fixed seeds everywhere; no wall-clock enters any number

A.provenance: pre-existing CSV (assumed generated with the module default seed 7; regenerate deterministically via `python ml/src/worldmodel.py --out ml/data/train.csv`)

B.provenance: pre-existing CSV (assumed generated with the module default seed 11; regenerate deterministically via `python ml/src/worldmodel2.py --out ml/data/train_v2.csv`)

A_to_B.unseen_note: every target-world row is unseen by the frozen source-world models: the worlds are separate generators with different seeds and different causal mechanisms, and nothing is retrained here

recovery.scored: P(recover | case, logged action_taken) vs realized `recovered`, on ALL target rows
recovery.in_world_ceiling_note: the target world's OWN calibrated primary scored on the same rows — PARTIALLY IN-SAMPLE (it trained on the earliest ~80% of them), so this is ceiling-only context, not a fair head-to-head
recovery.base_rate_note: Brier depends on the target world's base rate and the frozen calibration; compare within a direction, not across worlds

in_world_heldout_auc_at_train_time.note: the target world's own model on its own time-ordered held-out split (from train.py's metrics.json) — the fair in-world number

action_value.eval_split: time-ordered latest ~20% of target days — identical split, ground truth and bootstrap seed as the in-world eval.py run, so these numbers are directly comparable with eval.json / eval_v2.json; every case is still unseen by the frozen model
action_value.policy: frozen source-world CatBoost action head, argmax over pursuit actions, deployed hard-decline guard applied (eval.apply_policy_guard)

in_world_vs_rules.note: context: the TARGET world's own action head on the same cases — matches eval_v2.json incremental_lift_primary.vs_rules_only

action_value.rules_baseline_note: deterministic error-reason triage (eval.rules_only_action); every arm is graded by the TARGET world's ground-truth success_prob — models only CHOOSE actions, they never grade themselves
